8014cb12ab.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between śaniḥ and śukraḥ in rēvatī mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°36′15.67″.
8014cb12ab.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°36′15.67″, 0°36′02.25″ apart, disc-to-disc. śaniḥ at rēvatī-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°15′32.13″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.71, elongation 25°42′15.53″ W). śukraḥ at rēvatī-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°39′16.46″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.87, elongation 25°39′41.05″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
8014cb12ab.s:
bhāvābhāvāya lōkānāṁ kalpanēyaṁ pradarśitā।  
svamārgagāḥ prayāntyētē dūramanyōnyamāśritāḥ॥  
--sūryasiddhāntē  
  
ṣaṇmāsaṁ grahabhinnabhaṁ tyaja śubhē yauddhaṁ tathōtpātabham।  
--muhūrtacintāmaṇau (nāradasaṁhitānusārēṇa)

8128ce4237.s:
yaḥ mādhavē vaiśākhamāsē, trayōdaśīcaturdaśīpūrṇimāsu tithiṣu snānādikaṁ karōti  
sa niścayēna mōkṣaṁ prāpnuyāt। yathā purā dhanaśarmā brāhmaṇaḥ trayaḥ prētāśca  
muktiṁ prāpuriti। atra prasiddhā kathā saptadaśādhyāyātmakapādmōktavaiśākhamāhātmyē।  
purā viṣṇunā trayōdaśyāṁ hiraṇyākṣaḥ, caturdaśyāṁ madhuśca ghātitaḥ,  
paurṇamāsyāṁ bhūmyuddhāraśca kr̥taḥ, tataḥ prabhr̥ti tāstithayaḥ puṇyā jātāḥ!  
śrutadēva uvāca---  
yāstisrastithayaḥ puṇyā antimāḥ śuklapakṣakē।  
vaiśākhamāsi rājēndra pūrṇimāntāḥ śubhāvahāḥ॥1॥  
antyāḥ puṣkariṇīsaṁjñāḥ sarvapāpakṣayāvahāḥ।  
mādhavē māsi yaḥ pūrṇaṁ snānaṁ kartuṁ na ca kṣamaḥ॥2॥  
tithiṣvētāsu sa snāyātpūrṇamēva phalaṁ labhēt।  
sarvē dēvāstrayōdaśyāṁ sthitvā jantūnpunanti hi॥3॥  
pūrṇāyāḥ parvatīrthaiśca viṣṇunā saha saṁsthitāḥ।  
caturdaśyāṁ sayajñāśca dēvā ētānpunanti hi॥4॥  
brahmaghnaṁ vā surāpaṁ vā sarvānētānpunanti hi।  
ēkādaśyāṁ purā jajñē vaiśākhyāmamr̥taṁ śubham॥5॥  
dvādaśyāṁ pālitaṁ tacca viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā।  
trayōdaśyāṁ sudhāṁ dēvānpāyayāmāsa vai hariḥ॥6॥  
jaghāna ca caturdaśyāṁ daityāndēvavirōdhinaḥ।  
pūrṇāyāṁ sarvadēvānāṁ sāmrājyāptirbabhūva ha॥7॥  
tatō dēvāḥ susantuṣṭā ētāsāṁ ca varaṁ daduḥ।  
tisr̥ṇāṁ ca tithīnāṁ vai prītyōtphullavilōcanāḥ॥8॥  
ētā vaiśākhamāsasya tisraśca tithayaḥ śubhāḥ।  
putrapautrādiphaladā narāṇāṁ pāpahānidāḥ॥9॥  
yō'sminmāsē ca sampūrṇē na snātō manujādhamaḥ।  
tithitrayē tu sa snātvā pūrṇamēva phalaṁ labhēt॥10॥  
tithitrayē'pyakurvāṇaḥ snānadānādikaṁ naraḥ।  
cāṇḍālīṁ yōnimāsādya paścādrauravamaśnutē॥11॥  
uṣṇōdakēna yaḥ snāti mādhavē ca tithitrayē।  
rauravaṁ narakaṁ yāti yāvadindrāścaturdaśa॥12॥  
pitr̥̄ndēvānsamuddiśya dadhyannaṁ na dadāti yaḥ।  
paiśācīṁ yōnimāsādya tiṣṭhatyābhūtasamplavam॥13॥  
pravr̥ttānāṁ ca kāmānāṁ mādhavē niyamē kr̥tē।  
avaśyaṁ viṣṇusāyujyaṁ yujyatē nātra saṁśayaḥ॥14॥  
āmāsaṁ niyamāsaktaḥ kuryādyadi dinatrayē।  
tēna pūrṇaphalaṁ prāpya mōdatē viṣṇumandirē॥15॥  
yō vai dēvānpitr̥̄nviṣṇuṁ gurumuddiśya mānavaḥ।  
na snānādi karōtyaddhā'muṣya śāpapradā vayam॥16॥  
niḥsantānō nirāyuśca niḥśrēyaskō bhavēditi।  
iti dēvā varaṁ dattvā svadhāmāni yayuḥ purā॥17॥  
tasmāttithitrayaṁ puṇyaṁ sarvāghaughavināśanam।  
antyaṁ puṣkariṇīsaṁjñaṁ putrapautravivardhanam॥18॥  
yā nārī subhagā'pūpapāyasaṁ pūrṇimādinē।  
brāhmaṇāya sakr̥ddadyātkīrtimantaṁ sutaṁ labhēt॥19॥  
gītāpāṭhaṁ tu yaḥ kuryādantimē ca dinatrayē।  
dinēdinē'śvamēdhānāṁ phalamēti na saṁśayaḥ॥20॥  
sahasranāmapaṭhanaṁ yaḥ kuryyācca dinatrayē।  
tasya puṇyaphalaṁ vaktuṁ kaḥ śaktō divi vā bhuvi॥21॥  
sahasranāmabhirdēvaṁ pūrṇāyāṁ madhusūdanam।  
payasā snāpya vai yāti viṣṇulōkamakalmaṣam॥22॥  
samastavibhavairyastu pūjayēnmadhusūdanam।  
na tasya lōkāḥ kṣīyantē yuga kalpādi vyatyayē॥23॥  
asnātvā cāpyadattvā ca vaiśākhaśca matō yadi।  
sa brahmahā gurughnaśca pitr̥̄ṇāṁ ghātakastathā॥24॥  
ślōkārdhaṁ ślōkapādaṁ vā nityaṁ bhāgavatōdbhavam।  
vaiśākhē ca paṭhanmartyō brahmatvaṁ cōpapadyatē॥25॥  
yō vai bhāgavataṁ śāstraṁ śr̥ṇōtyētaddinatrayē।  
na pāpairlipyatē kvāpi padmapatramivāmbhasā॥26॥  
dēvatvaṁ manujaiḥ prāptaṁ kaiścitsiddhatvamēva ca।  
kaiścitprāptō brahmabhāvō dinatrayaniṣēvaṇāt॥27॥  
brahmajñānēna vai muktiḥ prayāgamaraṇēna vā।  
athavā māsi vaiśākhē niyamēna jalāplutēḥ॥28॥  
nīlavr̥ṣaṁ samutsr̥jya vaiśākhyāṁ ca jalāplutēḥ।  
samastabandhanirmuktaḥ pumānyāti paraṁ padam॥29॥  
gāṁ savatsāṁ dvijēndrāya sīdatē ca kuṭumbinē।  
ihāpamr̥tyunirmuktaḥ paratra ca paraṁ vrajēt॥30॥  
snānadānavihīnastu vaiśākhī caiva yō nayēt।  
śvānayōniśataṁ prāpya viṣṭhāyāṁ jāyatē kr̥miḥ॥31॥  
tisraḥ kōṭyō'rdhakōṭiśca tīrthāni bhuvanatrayē।  
sambhūya mantrayāñcakruḥ pāpasaṅghātaśaṅkitāḥ॥32॥  
janā asmāsu pāpiṣṭhā visr̥janti svakaṁ malam।  
tadasmākaṁ kathaṁ gacchēditi cintāsamanvitāḥ॥33॥  
tīrthapādaṁ hariṁ jagmuḥ śaraṇyaṁ śaraṇaṁ vibhum।  
stutvā ca bahubhiḥ stōtraiḥ prārthayāmāsurañjasā॥34॥  
dēvadēva jagannātha sarvāghaughavināśana।  
janā asmāsu pāpiṣṭhāḥ snātvā pāpāni sarvaśaḥ॥35॥  
visr̥jya tvatpadaṁ yānti tvadājñādhāriṇō bhuvi।  
asmākaṁ caiva tatpāpaṁ kathaṁ gacchējjanārdana॥36॥  
tadupāyaṁ vadāsmākaṁ tvatpādaśaraṇaiṣiṇām।  
iti tīrthaiḥ prārthitastu bhagavānbhūtabhāvanaḥ॥37॥  
prahasanprāha tīrthāni mēghagambhīrayā girā।  
śrībhagavānuvāca---  
sitē pakṣē mēṣasūryē vaiśākhāntēdinatrayē॥38॥  
sarvatīrthamayē puṇyē mamāpi prāṇavallabhē।  
yūyaṁ bhagōdayātpūrvaṁ bahiḥsaṁsthajalāplutāḥ॥39॥  
vimuktāghāḥ puṇyarūpā bhavantvāśu sunirmalāḥ।  
bhavadbhiśca vimuktāghairyē na snātā dinatrayē॥40॥

8131116431.d:
The Shukla-paksha Ekadashi of jyaiṣṭha month is known as pāṇḍava-nirjalā-ēkādaśī.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.

tāsāṁ phalamavāpnōti atra mē nāsti saṁśayaḥ॥ (hēmādrau-mahābhāratē vyāsavacanam)

yadīcchēdviṣṇusāyujyaṁ śriyaṁ santatimātmanaḥ।  
ēkādaśyāṁ na bhuñjīta pakṣayōrubhayōrapi॥  
  
adya sthitvā nirāhāraḥ śvōbhūtē paramēśvara।  
bhōkṣyāmi puṇḍarīkākṣa śaraṇaṁ mē bhavācyuta॥  
pramādādathavā''lasyāddharē kēśava mādhava।  
vratasyāsya ca vai vighnō na bhavēttvatprasādataḥ॥  
--padmapurāṇē

ēkādaśyāmanāhāraṁ gr̥hī vipraśca bhāratē।  
sa ca tiṣṭhati vaikuṇṭhē yāvadvai brahmaṇō vayaḥ॥14॥  
  
ēkādaśyupavāsaphalaṁ prōktaṁ pādmamahāpurāṇē---  
śaṅkhōddhārē naraḥ snātvā dr̥ṣṭvā dēvaṁ gadādharam॥35॥  
ēkādaśyupavāsasya kalāṁ nārhati ṣōḍaśīm।

ēkādaśyupavāsasya kalāṁ nārhati ṣōḍaśīm।  
prabhāsakṣētrē yatpuṇyaṁ grahaṇē candrasūryayōḥ॥37॥  
tatphalaṁ jāyatē nūnamēkādaśyupavāsinaḥ।  
kēdārē cōdakaṁ pītvā punarjanma na vidyatē॥38॥  
tathā caikādaśī pārtha garbhavāsakṣayaṅkarī।  
aśvamēdhasya yajñasya pr̥thivyāṁ yatphalaṁ labhēt॥39॥  
tasmācchataguṇaṁ puṇyamēkādaśyupavāsinaḥ।  
tapasvinō gr̥hē yasya bhuñjatē ca dvijōttamāḥ॥40॥  
tatphalaṁ jāyatē nūnamēkādaśyupavāsinaḥ।  
gōsahasrēṇa yatpuṇyaṁ datvā vēdāntapāragē॥41॥  
tasmācchataguṇaṁ puṇyamēkādaśyupavāsinaḥ।  
yēṣāṁ dēhē trayō dēvā brahmaviṣṇumahēśvarāḥ॥42॥  
vasanti tēṣāṁ tē tulyā ēkādaśyupavāsinaḥ।  
tē narāḥ puṇyakarmāṇō yē bhaktā haripūjakāḥ॥43॥  
ēkādaśīvratasyāpi puṇyasaṅkhyā na vidyatē।  
ētatpuṇyaṁ bhavēt tasya yatsurairapi durlabham॥44॥

82aac865d2.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in śravaṇaḥ makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′09.45″.
82aac865d2.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′09.45″, 0°41′02.09″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 2°00′23.81″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.28, elongation 5°47′39.57″ E). śukraḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°19′14.36″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 5°35′40.43″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

akṣayā sā tu samprōktā vyāsādyairmunipuṅgavaiḥ।  
tasmāttu karaṇaṁ yatsyāttacchr̥ṇudhvaṁ haripriyam॥3॥  
brāhmē muhūrtē cōtthāya cintayēdātmanō hitam।  
kr̥tvā nimittakaṁ karma pūjayēdiṣṭadēvatāḥ॥4॥  
viṣṇupūjāṁ vidhāyā''dau tathā pañcōpacārakaiḥ।  
pradadyāttatra naivēdyaṁ pakvānnaṁ salavaṅgakam॥5॥  
jīrakaṁ nāgaraṁ kr̥ṣṇamaricaṁ dāḍimaṁ tathā।  
nārikēlaphalaṁ cānyatkūṣmāṇḍakāñcanīyutam॥6॥  
saṅkalpya dadyācchrīkr̥ṣṇaḥ prīyatāmiti cākṣayaḥ।  
svaśaktyā tōṣayēdviprānnamaskārēṇa vā punaḥ॥7॥  
sūryagrahē kurukṣētrē tulādānasya yatphalam।  
tatphalaṁ labhatē martyastasyāṁ kūṣmāṇḍadānataḥ॥8॥  
mahāpātakayuktō'pi tadyuktō cōpapātakaiḥ।  
narō viśuddhamuktō hi yamalōkaṁ na paśyati॥9॥  
kūṣmāṇḍadānakartāraḥ sarvalōkānvrajanti vai।  
svēcchayā paryaṭantaśca nānābhōgaratā dvija॥10॥  
śaunaka uvāca---  
bhūlōkē kēna dattaṁ hi vada mahyaṁ munīśvara।  
dānaṁ kūṣmāṇḍakamayaṁ yēna kautūhalaṁ hi mē॥11॥  
nārada uvāca---  
antarvēdyāṁ mahāgrāmō yāmunasya girēradhaḥ।  
tatra subrāhmaṇō rāmaśarmā'sau lōkaviśrutaḥ॥12॥  
tēnātyantadhanaṁ samyagarjitaṁ pracuraṁ kila।  
puṇyakāryaparōdātā vārddhakyaṁ samupāgataḥ॥13॥  
tasya putrau tu sañjātau nāmnā kr̥ṣṇadhanañjayau।  
tayōrmūrddhavahaṁ dattvā jagāma tapasē vanam॥14॥  
tapaḥ kliṣṭaśarīrō'sau vāsudēvamanaḥ sadā।  
prāptavānvaiṣṇavaṁ sthānaṁ yatra gatvā na śōcati॥15॥  
tatastasya sutau tau tu kālē taruṇātāṁ gatau।  
vārastrīratisaṁsaktau madyapānaratau sadā॥16॥  
na śr̥ṇvatē vacaḥ pūrvaṁ vr̥ddhānāṁ tatra tāvubhau।  
parastrābhyaḥ pradadatuḥ sahasraṁ ca śataṁ tathā॥17॥  
ēvaṁ dravyaṁ kṣayaṁ nītaṁ tābhyāṁ kṣaṇasukhāya vai  
mallau cāṇūraśailūṣau vēśyādyutapriyāvubhau॥18॥  
apātrē taddhanaṁ dattaṁ bhuvi bījamivōṣarē।  
dravyakṣayādubhau bhūtau cauramārgānusāriṇau॥19॥  
rātrau tu kōṭapālēna dhr̥tā rājñā ca vāsitau।  
vanaṁ gatau tu tau sārdhamadharmaniratau dvijau॥20॥  
māṁsāhāriṇau sañjātau siṁhānmr̥tyumupāgatau।  
ēkasmindivasē brahmanmr̥tau yamapuraṁ gatau॥21॥  
yamadūtau tadā vākyaṁ kā śāstiḥ kriyatē vibhō।  
kiṅkarasya vacaḥ śrutvā tadā vaivasvatō yamaḥ॥22॥  
citraguptalēkhanīyaṁ narāṇāṁ ca śubhāśubham।  
ēkatra krōdhatāmrākṣaḥ ētau kutra kṣipāmyaham॥23॥  
citraguptō'bravīdvākyaṁ kiṅkarānśūladhāriṇaḥ।  
ēkaśca nīyatāṁ svargē yatra bhōgaśca śāśvatāḥ॥24॥  
aparō kṣipyatāṁ dūtā narakē yātanākulē।  
citraguptavacaḥ śrutvā tadā dūtaḥ priyaṁvadaḥ॥25॥  
nītvā dhanañjayaṁ tuṣṭaḥ svargamārgamupāgataḥ।  
anyastu pāpakarmāṇaṁ gr̥hītvā kr̥ṣṇaśarmakam॥26॥  
narakē'pātayatkruddhō bhuṅkṣva karmakr̥taṁ dvija।  
dhanañjayō vrajanmārgē paśyanvaicitryamāptavān॥27॥  
apsarāśca tadāgatya urvaśyādyā mahāmunē।  
pārijātakr̥tāṁ mālāṁ śirasi prākṣipanmudā॥28॥  
iti dr̥ṣṭvā tadāścaryaṁ svargamārgasya śaunaka।  
pr̥ṣṭavān yamadūtaṁ ca tadā sakaruṇaṁ vacaḥ॥29॥  
dhanañjaya uvāca---  
ēkā mātā pitā caikastābhyāṁ jātau sahōdarau।  
pāpamēva kr̥taṁ tābhyāṁ na vārtā puṇyakarmaṇaḥ॥30॥  
ēkasmindivasē dūta mr̥tau yamapurīṁ gatau।  
kathaṁ sa narakē kṣiptō mama jyēṣṭhaḥ priyaṁvada॥31॥  
mama bhāvī kathaṁ nātha saṁśayō'sti mahānmama।  
yamadūta uvāca---  
svasā mātā pitā bhrātā pitr̥vyaśca dhanañjaya।  
adr̥ṣṭakarmajā saṁjñā janmakarmōpabhuktayē॥32॥  
yathā kanyāgatē sūryē śvaśunīnāṁ samāgamaḥ।  
putrabhrātr̥pitr̥̄ṇāṁ ca tathā bhavati saṅgamaḥ॥33॥  
tasmāccintā na kartavyā vraja mārga purasya vai।  
puṇyavāṁstvaṁ sukr̥tināṁ lōkaṁ yāsi namō'stu tē॥34॥  
kēna puṇyēna māṁ dūta nayasi tvaṁ triviṣṭapam।  
pāpiṣṭhā matparō nānyō bhaviṣyati dharātalē॥35॥  
tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā yamadūtō'bravīdvacaḥ।  
pāṭhakasya prasaṅgēna gatastvaṁ yamunāṁ kila।  
vāsasī ca gurōrgr̥hya kuśāṁśca samidhastathā॥36॥  
ācāryasyājñayā snānamūrjē prātaḥ kr̥taṁ tryaham।  
niyamaṁ yatkr̥taṁ tatra sañjātastu mahatphalam॥37॥  
ēkēna majjēnanāśu pāpānmuktō'si janmanaḥ।  
majjanēna dvitīyēna akṣayaṁ svargamāpnuhi॥38॥  
narakē ca tava bhrātā sahatāṁ yamayātanām।  
iti śrutvā vacastasya bhrātr̥gauravayantritaḥ॥39॥  
dēvadūta praṇamyāhaṁ maitrīṁ sāptapadīṁ smaran।  
nirgamō narakād dūta bhrāturmē jāyatē katham॥40॥  
yathā'haṁ bhrātr̥saṅgēna svargaṁ yāmi priyaṁvada।  
na hi bhrātr̥samō bandhurna hi bhrātr̥samaḥ sakhā॥41॥  
na hi bhrātr̥samō trātā mātr̥jātaṁ viśēṣataḥ।  
svargaṁ nēcchē vinā tēna tatra mē kāryanirvr̥tiḥ॥42॥  
yathā bhrātā samō yōgastamupāyaṁ vadasva mē।  
iti śrutvā vacastasya dēvadūtō'bravīttataḥ॥43॥  
pūrvajanmakr̥taṁ puṇyaṁ tadvadāmi dhanañjaya।  
dānaṁ navamyāṁ kūṣmāṇḍasyōrjēśuklatithau dinē॥44॥  
sahiraṇyaṁ tvayā dattaṁ saratnaṁ ca savastrakam।  
dēhi puṇyaṁ ca tvaṁ bhrātrē duṣprāpyaṁ svargiṇāmapi॥45॥  
iti śrutvā vacastasya dēvadūtasya sādaram।  
dadau bhrātrē ca kūṣmāṇḍadānapuṇyaṁ dhanañjayaḥ॥46॥  
puṇyadānēna kr̥ṣṇō'pi narakādāgatastadā।  
bhrātrā saha dvijavaraḥ prāptavān vaiṣṇavaṁ padam॥47॥  
bhōgōpabhōgasampannau yamadūtavivarjitau।  
adyāpi tau dvijavarau puṇyaśīlasuśīlakau॥48॥  
kr̥ṣṇabhaktāvabhūtāṁ vai kr̥ṣṇārādhanatatparau।  
navamyāṁ kr̥ṣṇamuddiśya śuklapakṣē vicakṣaṇaiḥ॥49॥  
kārtikē māsi kūṣmāṇḍaṁ sahiraṇyaṁ savastrakam।  
kūṣmāṇḍasya ca dānēna tāryantē kōṭipūruṣāḥ॥50॥  
ētattē kathitaṁ vipra kārtikanavamīvratam।  
kūṣmāṇḍadānamāhātmyaṁ yadgītaṁ yamadūtakaiḥ॥51॥  
dhātryai caikapraṇāmēna aśvamēdhādhikaṁ phalam।  
pradakṣiṇāṁ tu kurutāṁ satyamētanmayōditam॥52॥  
brāhmaṇān satyasaṅghāṁśca haribhaktiparāyaṇān।  
bhuñjanti caiva yē viprāstēṣāmannaṁ guṇapradam॥53॥  
dhātricchāyāṁ samāśritya kārtikē'nnaṁ tu bhujyatē।  
annasaṁsargajaṁ pāpaṁ bahuvarṣaṁ ca naśyati॥54॥  
iti śrīpadmapurāṇē akṣayanavamīvratakathā samāptā॥  
  
atha kūṣmāṇḍadānavidhiḥ---  
kūṣmāṇḍadēvatāyai namaḥ iti gandhapuṣpaiḥ sampūjya dēśakālau saṅkīrtya amukagōtra amukaśarmā  
mama brahmahananādisamasta-pāpakṣaya-pūrvaka-bahuputra-śrī-saubhāgyādi-sakala-manōrathāvāpti-kūṣmāṇḍa-  
bīja-sasahasra-saṅkhyākābda-brahmalōka-viṣṇulōka-rudralōkanivāsakāmaḥ akṣayanavamī-yugādi-  
mahāparvanimattamidaṁ kūṣmāṇḍaphalaṁ bahubījāḍhyaṁ ghr̥taplutaṁ tilaliptaṁ suvarṇaphalaṁ tāmbūlavastrādiyuktaṁ  
gōdhūmarāśisthitaṁ vanaspatidaivataṁ dakṣiṇāyutaṁ yathānāmagōtrāya brāhmaṇāya dātumahamutsr̥jē॥  
brahmahatyādipāpaghnaṁ brahmaṇā nirmitaṁ purā।  
kūṣmāṇḍaṁ bahubījāḍhyaṁ putrapautrādivr̥ddhidam॥  
viṣṇavē namaḥ॥  
  
kārtikē śuklanavamī tatrā'bhūd dvāparaṁ yugam।  
pūrvā'parāhṇagā grāhyā kramād dānōpavāsayōḥ॥1॥  
atra kūṣmāṇḍakō nāma hatō daityastu viṣṇunā।  
tadrōmabhiḥ samudbhūtā vallyaḥ kūṣmāṇḍasambhavāḥ॥2॥  
tasmāt kūṣmāṇḍadānēna phalamāpnōti niścitam।  
---śrīskāndē mahāpurāṇē dvitīyē vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍē kārtikamāsamāhātmyē kūṣmāṇḍanavamītulasīvivāhavidhivarṇanaṁ nāmaikatriṁśō'dhyāyaḥ

847cde4c7f.d:
When Shravana nakshatra falls on a Monday, it is a special yōgaḥ. In the cyclic rotation of time, along with the bad combinations of grahas and nakshatras that indicate the probability of upcoming difficulties, good combinations that grant benefits in multiples also arise. Among such good combinations are the Amrita Siddhi yogas of certain weekdays and nakshatras. They are Sunday-Hasta, Monday-Mrigashirsha, Tuesday-Ashvini, Wednesday-Anuradha, Thursday-Pushya, Friday-Revati, Saturday-Rohini. Good deeds performed on such yogas become especially strong in protecting and nourishing us.
For instance, in Devi Atharvashirsha, it is said bhaumāśvinyāṁ mahādevī-sannidhau japtvā mahāmr̥tyuṁ tarati, that is, one can cross even mahāmr̥tyu by doing parayanam when Tuesday and Ashvini join.
847cde4c7f.s:
ādityahastē gurupuṣyayōgē budhānurādhā śanirōhiṇī ca।  
sōmē ca saumyaṁ bhr̥gurēvatī ca bhaumāśvinī cāmr̥tasiddhiyōgāḥ॥

84a1a70326.b: Observed on Śukla-Prathamā tithi of Āśvayujaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).

84a2acc4ca.d: When the transit of the Sun (saṅkrānti) happens in the second half of the day (aparāhṇa) and before midnight, the second half of the day form a puṇyakāla for various observances. In addition to 16 ghatikas on either side of the transition, and specific puṇyakālas like ṣaḍaśīti, viṣṇupadī etc., this is also useful, especially in cases where the other puṇyakālas are inconvenient for appropriate performance of rituals such as snāna, dāna, tarpaṇa, etc.

84a6542930.b: Observed on Paurṇamāsī tithi of Kārttikaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti).
84a6542930.s:
smr̥tyantarē---  
amā pātaśca saṅkrāntistathā vaidhr̥tirēva ca।  
aṣṭakāścaiva manvādiryugādiśca mahālayaḥ॥  
candrasūryōparāgaśca gajacchāyā tathaiva ca।  
dravyabrāhmaṇasampattiḥ śrāddhakālāḥ prakīrtitāḥ॥  
manvantarādayō matsyapurāṇē darśitāḥ---  
āśvayukchuklanavamī kārtikī dvādaśī sitā।  
tr̥tīyā caitramāsasya sitā bhādrapadasya ca॥  
phālgunasyāpyamāvāsyā puṣyasyaikādaśī sitā।  
āṣāḍhasyāpi daśamī māghamāsasya saptamī॥  
śrāvaṇasyāṣṭamī kr̥ṣṇā tathā''ṣāḍhī ca pūrṇimā।  
kārtikī phālgunī caitrī jyaiṣṭhī pañcadaśī sitā॥  
manvantarādayaścaitē dattasyākṣayakārakāḥ।  
kr̥taṁ śrāddhaṁ vidhānēna manvādiṣu yugādiṣu॥  
hāyanāni dvisāhasraṁ pitr̥̄ṇāṁ tr̥ptidaṁ bhavēt।  
āsu snānaṁ japō hōmaḥ puṇyānantyāya kalpatē॥  
mahābhāratē'pi---   
yā manvādyā yugādyāśca tithayastāsu mānavaḥ।  
snātvā bhuktvā ca dattvā ca tadanantaphalaṁ labhēt॥  
kālādarśē'pi---  
manvādyāsu yugādyāsu pradattaḥ salilāñjaliḥ।  
sahasravārṣikī tr̥ptiṁ pitr̥̄ṇāmāvahēt parām॥  
dvisahasrābdikī tr̥ptiṁ kr̥taṁ śrāddhaṁ yathāvidhi।  
snānaṁ dānaṁ japō hōmaḥ puṇyānantyāya kalpatē॥  
puruṣārthacintāmaṇau manuḥ---  
sahasraguṇitaṁ dānaṁ bhavēddattaṁ yugādiṣu।  
karma śrāddhādikaṁ caiva tathā manvantarādiṣu॥

84be232db0.b: Observed on Śukla-Saptamī tithi of Āśvayujaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 4162 (Kali era).
84be232db0.d: Śrīkaṇṭha, son of Śivasāmbapaṇḍita, known by the appellation Parāśiva (Paramaśiva) (after initiation) who remained in the caves of the mountain since initiation governed the Pīṭha for twenty-one years and having placed poet Somaka’s son, Sūrya, in his place, He attained siddhi in the night of saptami of the bright fortnight in the Aśvini month of the year Śārvari. This preceptor Paramaśivendra stayed in the caves of Sahya mountain adhering to the “mode of python” (ajagaravṛtti), restored to by the disciple named Bodhendra, attained siddhi in the Sahya mountain itself.
84be232db0.s:
śrīkaṇṭhaḥ śivasāmbapaṇḍitasutaḥ saikāṁ samā viṁśatiṁ  
bibhrat svasya padē nivēśya sukaviṁ sūryātmajaṁ sōmakam।  
śārvaryāśvinasaptamīniśi gataḥ siddhiṁ sa pakṣē sitē  
sannyāsāt prabhr̥ti kṣitidhra-vivara-sthāyī parādiḥ śivaḥ॥88॥  
—puṇyaślōkamañjarī

84fe129f13.d:
The celestial wedding of Bhagavan Srinivasa and Devi Padmavati is a grand festival held annually in the month of Vaishakha. The beautifully adorned Parinayotsavam Mandapam, set amidst the Narayanagiri gardens, serves as the enchanting venue for this three-day event, celebrated under the moonlit sky. The festivities unfold on the auspicious days of Navami, Dashami, and Ekadashi in the month of Vaishakha, featuring Sri Malayappaswami, Shri Venkateshwara's festival deity. Each day, he makes a grand entrance on different Vahanas: the Gaja (elephant), Ashva (horse), and Garuda (eagle), while Devi-s Sridevi and Bhudevi grace the event on separate palanquins.

Following the wedding rituals at the Parinayotsava Mandapam, a traditional 'Koluvu' gathering takes place, filled with the recitation of Vedic hymns and devotional songs. Bhagavan, accompanied by Sridevi and Bhudevi, then majestically returns to the temple.

Each day's festivities are marked by unique traditional rituals. On the first day, the arrival of Bhagavan Malayappa Swami on the celestial Gaja Vahanam, along with his consorts on their palanquins, is a sight to behold. The traditional wedding ceremony is conducted, where Bhagavan is seated in the ornately decorated Parinaya Mandapam, with his consorts positioned opposite him.

The ceremony includes several traditional rituals such as Edurukolu (mutual reception), Pula Bantata (game of flower balls), and Vastra Dharanam (offering of new clothes). These customs are observed over all three days. The grand finale of the divine marriage is marked by a spectacular display of fireworks, adding to the ceremony's splendor. The event concludes with a procession where Bhagavan Malayappa Swami, along with Devi-s Sridevi and Bhudevi, return to the main temple.

876d1091f6.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Mangaiyarkarasiyar, the 50th of the Nayanmars was the wife of another Nayanmar, Ninra Seer Nadumara Nayanmar, who was earlier known as Koon Pandyan, the hunchbacked Pandyan king of Madurai. Tiru Jnana Sambandar, a revered Nayanmar, arrived in Madurai and was invited into the city by Kulacchirai Nayanmar. Despite attempts by the Jains to harm Sambandar, his divine singing miraculously cured the king of his hunchback and alleviated his pain, leading to his return to Shaivism. Following his conversion, the king conquered northern kings at Tirunelveli, spreading Shaivism in those regions with the support of his wife. Both he and Mangayarkarasiyar deeply revered Sambandar and their dedication to their guru and Shaivism ultimately brought them divine grace.
876d1091f6.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

876f0fd942.d:
The Phalguna Paurnami festival is a grand five-day celebration held annually at the Swami Pushkarini. Each day of the festival features a different set of deities taken for a celestial ride on a beautifully decorated float in the temple tank.

1. On the first day, Bhagavan Rama, along with Sita and Lakshmana, are worshipped and taken for a ride on the float.
2. The second day is dedicated to Bhagavan Krishna and Rukmini, who are also offered puja and taken on the float for a pleasure ride.

For the last three days, from Trayodashi to Paurnami:
1. Sri Malayappa Swami, accompanied by Sridevi and Bhudevi, are taken out for a ride in the temple tank.
2. The third day includes three rounds of the float, increasing to five rounds on the next day.
3. On the final day, the utsava murtis (festival deities) are taken for a splendid ride on the float for seven rounds, attracting a large number of pilgrims. The beauty of the deities is further enhanced by the charm of the full moon, making this day particularly special and visually stunning.

8a80989174.d: It is said in Vishnu Purāṇam that when Amavasya overlaps with one of nine nakshatras---Anuradha, Vishakha, Swati, Pushya, Ardra, Punarvasu, Shravishtha, Purvaproshthapada, or Shatabhishak---it is sacred even for Devas. For instance, Shraaddha done on an Amavasya joined with Anuradha, Vishakha, Swati keeps the pitrs satisfied for eight years. Likewise, on Pushya, Ardra and Punarvasu, the pitrs are satisfied for twelve years. It is said in the Smrtis, that if Amavasya falls on a Monday, Tuesday or Thursday, such a tithi is given the appellation puṣkalā and is as sacred as a solar eclipse. amāvāsyā of māgha month.

kaṣṭānmāṁ mōcayēśāna sarvamiṣṭaṁ ca dēhi mē॥  
  
yadā saṅklēśitō martyō nānāduḥkhaiśca dāruṇaiḥ।  
tadā kr̥ṣṇē caturthyāṁ vai pūjanīyō gaṇādhipaḥ॥ (bhaviṣyapurāṇam)  
nāradīyapurāṇē 113.60---

8cc1588acf.d: Chaturthī tithi on a Tuesday is as sacred as a solar eclipse. When it occurs in śuklapakṣa, it is called sukhā. Good day for doing puja of Ganesha/Subrahmanya with naivedyam of modakam/millet flour respectively.
8cc1588acf.s:
sumanturuvāca---  
sukhāvahā ca susukhā saubhāgyakaraṇī param॥11॥  
caturthī kuruśārdūla rūpasaubhāgyadā śubhā।  
sukhāvrataṁ mahāpuṇyaṁ rūpadaṁ bhāgyadaṁ tathā॥12॥  
susūkṣmaṁ sukaraṁ dhanyamiha puṇyasukhāvaham।  
paratra phaladaṁ vīra divyarūpapradāyakam॥13॥  
hasitaṁ lalitaṁ cōktaṁ cēṣṭitaṁ ca sukhāvaham।  
savilāsabhujakṣēpaṁ caṅkramaṁ cēṣṭitaṁ śubham॥14॥  
sukhāvratēna sarvēṣāṁ sukhaṁ kurukulōdvaha।  
kr̥tyēna pūjitē cēśē vighnēśē śivayōḥ sutē॥15॥  
yadā śuklacaturthyāṁ tu vārō bhaumasya vai bhavēt।  
tadā sā sukhadā jñēyā caturthī vai sukhēti ca॥16॥  
purā maithunamāśritya sthitābhyāṁ tu himācalē।  
bhīmōmābhyāṁ mahābāhō raktabinduścyutaḥ kṣitau॥17॥  
mēdinyāṁ sa prayatnēna sukhēna vidhr̥tō'nayā।  
jātō'syāḥ sa kujō vīra raktō raktasamudbhavaḥ॥18॥  
mamāṅgatō yathōtpannastasmādaṅgārakō hyayam।  
aṅgadō'ṅgōpakāraśca aṅgānāṁ tu pradō nr̥ṇām॥19॥  
saubhāgyādikarō yasmāttasmādaṅgārakō mataḥ।  
bhaktyā caturthyāṁ naktēna yō vai śraddhāsamanvitaḥ॥20॥  
upōṣyati narō rājannārī vā nānyamānasā।  
pūjayēcca kujaṁ bhaktyā raktapuṣpavilēpanaiḥ॥21॥  
gaṇēśaṁ prathamaṁ bhaktyā yō'rcayēcchraddhayānvitaḥ।  
yasya tuṣṭaḥ prayacchētsa saubhāgyaṁ rūpasampadam॥22॥  
pūrvaṁ ca kr̥tasaṅkalpaḥ snānaṁ kr̥tvā yathāvidhi।  
gr̥hītvā mr̥ttikāṁ vandēnmantrēṇānēna bhārata॥23॥  
iha tvaṁ vanditā pūrvaṁ kr̥ṣṇēnōddharatā kila।  
tasmānmē daha pāpmānaṁ yanmayā pūrvasañcitam॥24॥  
imaṁ mantraṁ paṭhanvīra ādityāya pradarśayēt।  
ādityaraśmisampūtāṁ gaṅgājalakaṇōkṣitām॥25॥  
dattvā mr̥daṁ śirasi tāṁ sarvāṅgēṣu ca yōjayēt।  
tataḥ snānaṁ prakurvīta mantrayēta jalaṁ punaḥ॥26॥  
tvamāpō yōniḥ sarvēṣāṁ daityadānavadyaukasām।  
svēdāṇḍajōdbhidāṁ caiva rasānāṁ patayē namaḥ॥27॥  
snātō'haṁ sarvatīrthēṣu sarvaprasravaṇēṣu ca।  
taḍāgēṣu ca sarvēṣu mānasādisaraḥsu ca॥28॥  
nadīṣu dēvakhātēṣu sutīrthēṣu hradēṣu vai।  
dhyāyan paṭhannimaṁ mantraṁ tataḥ snānaṁ samācarēt॥29॥  
tataḥ snātvā śucirbhūtvā gr̥hamāgatya vai spr̥śēt।  
dūrvāśvatthau śamīṁ spr̥ṣṭvā gāṁ ca mantrēṇa mantravit॥30॥  
dūrvā namasya mantrēṇa śucau bhūmau samutthitām।  
tvaṁ dūrvē'mr̥tanāmāsi sarvadēvaistu vanditā॥31॥  
vanditā daha tatsarvaṁ duritaṁ yanmayā kr̥tam॥32॥  
śamīmantraṁ pravakṣyāmi tannibōdha mahīpatē।  
pavitrāṇāṁ pavitrāṁ tvaṁ kāśyapī prathitā śrutau।  
śamī śamaya mē pāpaṁ nūnaṁ vētsi dharādharān॥33॥  
aśvatthālambhanē vīra mantramētaṁ nibōdha mē।  
nētraspandādijaṁ duḥkhaṁ duḥsvapnaṁ durvicintanam।  
śaktānāṁ ca samudyōgamaśvattha tvaṁ kṣamasva mē॥34॥  
imaṁ mantraṁ paṭhanvīra kuryādvai sparśanaṁ budhaḥ।  
tatō dēvyai tu gāṁ dadyādvīraṁ kr̥tvā pradakṣiṇām।  
samālabhya tu hastēna tatō mantramudīrayēt॥35॥  
sarvadēvamayī dēvi munibhistu supūjitā।  
tasmātspr̥śāmi vandē tvāṁ vanditā pāpahā bhava॥36॥  
imaṁ mantraṁ paṭhanvīra bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ।  
pradakṣiṇaṁ tu yaḥ kuryādarjunaṁ kurunandana।  
pradakṣiṇīkr̥tā tēna pr̥thivī syānna saṁśayaḥ॥37॥  
ēvaṁ maunēna cā''gatya tatō vahnigr̥haṁ vrajēt।  
prakṣālya ca mr̥dā pādāvācāntōgnigr̥haṁ viśēt।  
hōmaṁ tatra prakurvīta ēbhirmantrapadairvaraiḥ॥38॥  
śarvāya śarvaputrāya kṣōṇyutsaṅgabhavāya ca।  
kujāya lalitāṅgāya lōhitāṅgāya vai tathā॥39॥  
ōṁkārapūrvakairmantraiḥ svāhākārasamanvitaiḥ।  
aṣṭōttaraśataṁ vīra ardhārdhamardhamēva ca॥40॥  
ētairmantrapadairbhaktyā śaktyā vā kāmatō nr̥pa।  
khādiraiḥ susamidbhistu cā''jyadugdhairyavaistilaiḥ॥41॥  
bhakṣyairnānāvidhaiścānyaiḥ śaktyā bhaktyā samanvitaḥ।  
hutvā''hutīstatō vīra dēvaṁ saṁsthāpayētkṣitau॥42॥  
sauvarṇaṁ rājataṁ vā'pi śaktyā dārumayaṁ nr̥pa।  
dēvadārumayaṁ vā'pi śrīkhaṇḍacandanairapi॥43॥  
tāmrē pātrē raupyamayē cā''jyakuṅkumakēsaraiḥ।  
anyairvā lōhitairvā'pi puṣpaiḥ patraiḥ phalairapi।  
raktaiśca vividhairvīra atha vā śaktitō'rcayēt॥44॥  
yāvadvisr̥jatē vittaṁ vittavānvīra bhaktitaḥ।  
tāvadvivardhatē puṇyaṁ dātuṁ śatasahasrikam॥45॥  
anyē tāmramayē pātrē vaṁśajē mr̥nmayē'pi vā।  
pūjayanti narāḥ śaktyā kr̥tvā kuṅkumakēsaraiḥ।  
puruṣākr̥tikr̥taṁ pātra imaṁ mantraiḥ samarcayēt॥46॥  
agrirmūrdhēti mantrēṇa gandhapuṣpādibhistathā।  
dhūpairabhyarcya vidhivadbrāhmaṇāya pradīyatē॥47॥  
guḍaudanaṁ ghr̥taṁ kṣīraṁ gōdhūmāñchālitaṇḍulān।  
avēkṣya śaktiṁ dadyādvai daridrō vittavāṁstathā॥48॥  
vittaśāṭhyaṁ na kartavyaṁ vidyamānē dhanē nr̥pa।  
vittaśāṭhyaṁ hi kurvāṇō nāmutra phalabhāgbhavēt॥49॥  
śatānīka uvāca  
aṅgārakēṇa saṁyuktā caturthī naktabhōjanaiḥ।  
upōṣyā katimātrā tu utāhō sakr̥dēva tu॥50॥  
sumanturuvāca  
caturthī sā caturthī sā yadāṅgārakasaṁyutā।  
upōṣyā tatra tatraiva pradēyō vidhivadguḍaḥ॥51॥  
upōṣya naktēna vibhō catasraḥ kujasaṁyutā।  
caturthyāṁ ca caturthyāṁ ca vidhānaṁ śr̥ṇu yādr̥śam॥52॥  
sauvarṇaṁ tu kujaṁ kr̥tvā savināyakamādarāt।  
daśasauvarṇikaṁ mukhyaṁ daśārdhamardhamēva ca॥53॥  
sauvarṇapātrē raupyē vā bhaktyā tāmramayē'pi vā।  
viṁśatpalāni pātrāṇi viṁśatyardhapalāni vā॥54॥  
viṁśatkarṣāṇi vā vīra viṁśadardhārdhamēva vā।  
raupyasaṅkhyaṁ palaṁ kāryaṁ palārdhamardhamēva ca॥55॥  
śaktyā vittaiśca bhaktyā ca pātrē tāmramayē'pi tu।  
pratiṣṭhāpya grahēśaṁ vai vastraiḥ samparivēṣṭitam।  
vividhaiḥ sādhakai raktaiḥ puṣpai raktaiḥ samanvitam॥56॥  
brāhmaṇāya sadā dadyāddakṣiṇāsahitaṁ nr̥pa।  
vācakāya mahābāhō guṇinē śrēyasē nr̥pa॥57॥  
iti tē kathitā puṇyā tithīnāmuttamā tithiḥ।  
yāmupōṣya narō rūpaṁ divyamāpnōti bhārata॥58॥  
kāntyā''trēyasamaṁ vīraṁ tējasā ravisannibham।  
prabhayā ravikalpaṁ ca samīrabalasaṁśritam॥59॥  
īdr̥grūpaṁ samāpyēha yāti bhaumasadō nr̥pa।  
prasādādvighnanāthasya tathā gaṇapatērnr̥pa॥60॥  
paṭhatāṁ śr̥ṇvatāṁ rājankurvatāṁ ca viśēṣataḥ।  
brahmahatyādipāpāni kṣīyantē nātra saṁśayaḥ।  
r̥ddhiṁ vr̥ddhiṁ tathā lakṣmīṁ labhatē nātra saṁśayaḥ॥61॥  
---śrībhaviṣyē mahāpurāṇē śatārdhasāhasryāṁ saṁhitāyāṁ brāhmē parvaṇi caturthīkalpē sukhāvahāṅgārakacaturthīvratanirūpaṇaṁ nāmaikatriṁśō'dhyāyataḥ

8d4e35aad0.d: Dvadashi tithi, which starts after sunrise on a day and ends before sunrise on the next. O brāhmaṇa, merely hearing the account of Trispṛśā, which is both wonderful and thrilling, grants the religious merit equivalent to bathing in the Gaṅgā. Fasting on Trispṛśā yields the same rewards as performing thousands of Aśvamedha sacrifices and hundreds of Vājapeya sacrifices. It brings liberation not only to oneself but also to one's paternal, maternal, and personal family lines, and one is honoured in the world of Viṣṇu. The merit obtained from fasting on Trispṛśā is equal to that of visiting millions of holy and sacred places. O noble brāhmaṇa, all those—whether they are brāhmaṇas, evil-minded kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, or persons of other jātis—achieve salvation after leaving the earth. This vow is the king of all vows, much like how the revered dvādaśākṣarī is, among mantras. It is the foremost of vows for those who observe it. It was first followed by Brahmā and then by royal sages. What more can be said? Trispṛśā bestows (even) salvation.
8d4e35aad0.s:
mahādēva uvāca---  
dvijaitat trispr̥śākhyānamadbhutaṁ rōmaharṣaṇam।  
śrutvā tu labhatē puṇyaṁ gaṅgātīrthaphalaṁ labhēt॥78॥  
aśvamēdhasahasrāṇi vājapēyaśatāni ca।  
tatphalaṁ samavāpnōti trispr̥śāsamupōṣaṇāt॥79॥  
pitr̥pakṣō mātr̥pakṣastathā caivātmapakṣakaḥ।  
taiḥ sarvaiḥ saha sambhuktō viṣṇulōkē mahīyatē॥80॥  
tīrthakōṭiṣu yatpuṇyaṁ kṣētrakōṭiṣu yatphalam।  
tatphalaṁ samavāpnōti trispr̥śāsamupōṣaṇāt॥81॥  
brāhmaṇā yē'pi kurvanti kṣatriyāḥ kr̥ṣṇamānasāḥ।  
vaiśyā vā śūdrajanmānō yē tathā cānyajātayaḥ॥82॥  
tē sarvē muktimāyānti bhuvaṁ tyaktvā dvijōttama।  
mantrāṇāṁ mantrarājō'tha yathā syād dvādaśākṣaraḥ॥83॥  
vratānāṁ ca yathā caiṣā yēna vai trispr̥śā kr̥tā।  
brahmaṇā ca kr̥tā pūrvaṁ paścādrājarṣibhiḥ kr̥tā॥84॥  
anyēṣāṁ kā kathā vatsa trispr̥śā muktidāyinī।  
---śrīpādmē mahāpurāṇa uttarakhaṇḍa umāpatināradasaṁvādē trispr̥śākhyānaṁ nāma pañcatriṁśō'dhyāyaḥ॥35॥  
kr̥tyasārasamuccayē kārtikamāsakr̥tyē smr̥ti-vacanam---  
ēkādaśī dvādaśī ca rātriśēṣē trayōdaśī।  
tryahaspr̥śamahōrātraṁ tatra sāhasrikaṁ phalam॥ iti। sāhasrikaṁ sahasraguṇam।

8dcec7f554.b: Observed on Viśākhā nakshatra of Makaraḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
8dcec7f554.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

The 2nd of these Nayanmars was tirunīlakaṇṭha nāyanmār, a dedicated devotee of Bhagavan Shiva who lived in Chidambaram, and was a potter by profession. He revered Bhagavan Shiva's devotees and often gifted them with clay begging bowls he crafted, finding great joy in this service.

Tiru Neelakanta Nayanmar worshipped Bhagavan Shiva in his form as Neelakanta, drawing inspiration from the deity's act of consuming poison to protect the world. He believed fervently that those who sought refuge in Bhagavan Shiva would be absolved of their sins and attain His divine abode.

Despite his virtuous life, Neelakanta once succumbed to lust and visited a prostitute. His pious wife discerned this but chose to serve him as usual, resolving privately to abstain from sexual relations with him. When Neelakanta approached her passionately, she swore by Bhagavan Neelakanta and inadvertently used “us” instead of “me”. Taking her words to heart and their vow to Bhagavan Shiva, Neelakanta decided never to touch any woman again, a testament to his deep devotion.

The couple lived on, keeping their vow secret. As they aged, Bhagavan Shiva chose to unveil Neelakanta's spiritual greatness. Disguised as a Shiva Yogi, Bhagavan Shiva entrusted Neelakanta with a special bowl, claiming it could purify anything it touched. Later, when Bhagavan Shiva returned for the bowl, he miraculously made it disappear, leading Neelakanta to admit its loss. Accused of theft and unable to touch his wife due to their vow, the situation escalated to a court hearing.

At the court, Neelakanta revealed their secret of celibacy. As they held the ends of a stick and immersed themselves in a tank, a miracle occurred. They emerged youthful and radiant. Bhagavan Shiva and Mother Parvathy then appeared, declaring that due to their self-control and devotion, Neelakanta and his wife would live eternally youthful in the divine abode. This story showcases the power of devotion, celibacy, and the unassuming nature of true virtue.

8e133deb86.b: Observed on day 2 of Karkaṭaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
8e133deb86.d: One must not bathe in many (small) rivers during the rainy season. Especially for the first three days of Karkataka masa, these rivers are impure. However, this does not apply to the Mahanadis, owing to their greatness, including Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Godavari, Kaveri, Shona, Penna, and the Pancha Gangas (Kaveri, Tungabhadra, Krishnaveni, Gautami, Bhagirathi). Exceptions are made in the case of Upakarma, Utsarga, Grahanam, Preta snanam etc., and when new water can be mixed in these rivers, and when there is a lack of other water sources.
8e133deb86.s:
atriḥ---  
siṁhakarkaṭayōrmadhyē sarvā nadyō rajasvalāḥ।  
na snānādīni karmāṇi tāsu kurvīta mānavaḥ॥  
yōgayājñavalkyaḥ---  
rajōduṣṭē'mbhasi snānaṁ varjyaṁ nadyādiṣu dvijaiḥ।  
kadarthitaṁ rajastēṣāṁ sandhyōpāstiśca tarpaṇam  
vyāghrapādaḥ---  
siṁhakarkaṭayōrmadhyē sarvā nadyō rajasvalāḥ।  
tāsu snānaṁ na kurvīta varjayitvā samudragāḥ॥  
kātyāyanaḥ---  
karkaṭādau rajōduṣṭā gōmatī vāsaratrayam।  
candrabhāgā satī sindhuḥ sarayūnarmadā tathā॥  
atrāpavādamāha marīciḥ---  
ādityaduhitā gaṅgā plakṣajātā sarasvatī।  
rajasā nābhibhūyantē yē cānyē nadasaṁjñitāḥ॥  
mārkaṇḍēyaḥ---  
kālindī gautamī gaṅgā vēṇikā ca sarasvatī।  
sāmarthyādābhijātyāca rajō nābhibhavatyamūḥ॥  
jāhnavyādityasambhūtā plakṣajātā sarasvatī।  
rajasā naiva duṣyanti nadāḥ kr̥ṣṇā ca vēṇikā॥  
vāmanapurāṇē---  
sarasvatī nadī puṇyā tathā vaitaraṇī nadī।  
āpagā ca mahāpuṇyā gaṅgā mandākinī tathā॥  
madhupravāhāṁ'śumatī kauśikī pāpanāśinī।  
dr̥ṣadvatī mahāpuṇyā tathā vaitaraṇī nadī॥  
ētāsāmudakaṁ puṇyaṁ varṣākālē pravarddhitam।  
rajasvalātvamētāsāṁ vidyatē na kadācana॥  
yamaḥ---  
gaṅgā dharmōdbhavā puṇyā yamunā ca sarasvatī।  
antargatarajōyōgāḥ sarvāhaḥsvapi cāmalāḥ॥  
kālādarśaḥ---  
siṁhakarkaṭayōrnadyaḥ sarvā ēva rajasvalāḥ।  
tridinaṁ syurmahānadyō gōdāṁ pēṇṇāṁ sarasvatīm।  
bhāgīrathīṁ ca kālindī nadān śōṇādikān vinā॥  
kēcittu–--  
yā nissr̥tā nadāḥ prōktā yāśca gaṅgēti kīrtitāḥ।  
ētāsāṁ karkaṭē bhānau rajōdōṣō na vidyatē॥  
kāvērītuṅgabhadrā ca kr̥ṣṇavēṇī ca gautamī।  
bhāgīrathī ca vikhyātā pañcagaṅgāḥ prakīrtitāḥ॥  
kātyāyanaḥ---  
upākarmaṇi cōtsargē prētasnānē tathaiva ca।  
candrasūryagrahē caiva rajōdōṣō na vidyatē॥  
mahadambusamaṁ vā'pi yadi tiṣṭhēt purātanam।  
navāmbu miśritaṁ tēna na duṣṭamiti sūrayaḥ॥   
vyāghrapādaḥ---  
abhāvē kūpavāpīnāmanapāyipayōbhr̥tām।  
rajōduṣṭē'pi payasi grāmabhōgō na duṣyati॥

8e2763ab93.b: Observed on Śukla-Caturdaśī tithi of Mārgaśīrṣaḥ (lunar) month (Pūrvāhṇaḥ/paraviddha).
8e2763ab93.d: O great ascetic, today, on the fourteenth tithi of the bright half, in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, The bathing and other rites performed here lead to the deliverance from the state of a Pishācha. Having bathed near Kapardīśvara on the fourteenth tithi of the bright half of Mārgaśīrṣa, And dying even elsewhere, one does not attain the state of a Pishacha. Those humans who perform this annual journey (yātrā), Will overcome the sins incurred by accepting gifts/fees at a sacred place (tīrtha-pratigrahāt pāpāt). Having bathed at the Pishācha-Mochana Tīrtha, and having duly worshipped Kapardīśa (https://maps.app.goo.gl/tnyPhvCrr4etPC7o7), And having performed the offering of food (annadāna), one becomes fearless both here (in this world) and hereafter. At the Pishācha-Mochana Tīrtha, one should raise/take a 'loṣṭadroṇa' [a measure/amount of water]—in the other world, they are not tormented even by a slight thirst. Thus, the Pishācha-Mochana Yātrā (pilgrimage) is described by the verses of the Skanda Sanatkumāra Saṃhitā in the work Kāśī-Tattva-Prakāśikā. Since the tithis of the forenoon (pūrvāhṇa) are auspicious for rites concerning the gods, the Chaturdashī (fourteenth tithi) that prevails in the forenoon is to be taken for the observance of this yātrā.
8e2763ab93.s:
mārgaśuklacaturdaśyām---  
adya śuklacaturdaśyāṁ mārgē māsi tapōnidhē।  
atra sānādikaṁ kārya paiśācyaparimōcanam॥  
mārgaśuklacaturdaśyāṁ kapardīśvarasannidhau।  
mātvā'nyatrāpi maraṇānna paiśācyamavāpnuyāt॥  
imāṁ sāṁvatsarī yātrā yē kariṣyanti mānavāḥ।  
tīrthapratigrahāt pāpāt tē tariṣyanti mānavāḥ॥  
paiśācamōcanē snātvā kapardīśaṁ samarcya ca।  
kr̥tvā tatrānnadānaṁ ca ihāmutra ca nirbhayaḥ॥  
piśācamōcanē tīrthē lōṣṭadrōṇaṁ samuddharēt।  
na pīḍyatē parē lōkē svalpayā'pi pipāsayā॥  
iti kāśītattvaprakāśikāyāṁ skāndasanatkumārasaṁhitāvacanaiḥ piśācamōcanayātrōktā। tatra  
``paurvāhṇikāstu tithayō dēvakāryē śubhapradāḥ॥'' itivacanātpaurvāhṇikī caturdaśī grāhyā।

8f0b99f616.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Dvitīyā tithi of Bhādrapadaḥ (lunar) month (Chandrōdayaḥ/paraviddha).
8f0b99f616.d: Bhagavan Mahavishnu sleeps with Devi Mahalakshmi on this day. Do Puja by placing Bhagavan/Devi on a new bed with pillow/blanket. Do danam of same after puja.
8f0b99f616.s:
madanaratnē bhaviṣyē---  
śrīkr̥ṣṇa uvāca---  
śētē jagatpatiḥ kr̥ṣṇaḥ śriyā sārdhaṁ yadā nr̥pa।  
aśūnyaśayanā nāma tadā grāhyā tu sā tithiḥ॥  
kr̥ṣṇapakṣē dvitīyāyāṁ śrāvaṇē māsi bhārata।  
(asmin vratē śrāvaṇaḥ śuklāntō grāhyaḥ।)  
vāmanapurāṇē---  
dvādaśyāditithiṣu kramēṇa śrīkr̥ṣṇa-kāma-yakṣō-māpati-brahma-viśvakarmaṇāṁ svāpamabhidhāya---  
yasyāṁ tithyāṁ prasvapiti viśvakarmā prajāpatiḥ।  
dvitīyā sā śubhā puṇyā supuṇyaśayanōcitā॥  
tasyāṁ tithāvarcya hariṁ śrīvatsāṅkaṁ caturbhajam।  
paryaṅkasthaṁ samaṁ lakṣmyā gandhapuṣpādibhirmunē॥  
tatō dēvāya śayyāyāṁ phalāni prakṣipētkramāt।  
ityādinā āṣāḍhyavyavahitadvitīyāyāmēvābhidhānāt।  
imamuccārayēnmantraṁ praṇamya ca jagatpatim---  
śrīvatsadhāri śrīkānta śrīvāsa śrīpatē'vyaya।  
gārhasthyaṁ mā praṇāśaṁ mē yātu dharmārthakāmadam॥  
śucayō mā praṇaśyantu mā praṇaśyantu nirjarāḥ।  
yāmyagā mā praṇaśyantu mattō dampatyabhēdataḥ॥  
(śucayō'gnayaḥ। nirjarā dēvāḥ। yāmyagāḥ pitaraḥ।)  
lakṣmyā viyujyatē dēva na kadācidyathā bhavān।  
tathā kalatrasambandhō dēva mā mē viyujyatām॥  
lakṣmyā na śūnyaṁ varada yathā tē śayanaṁ sadā।  
śayyā mamāpyaśūnyāstu tathā'tra madhusūdana।  
viṣṇurahasyē tu---  
patnī bharturviyōgaṁ ca bhartā bhāryāsamudbhavam।  
nāpnuvanti yathā duḥkhaṁ dampatyāni tathā kuru॥  
yathā śriyā yutō viṣṇurlakṣmīrdēva tvayā yathā।  
prasādāttava dēvēśa bhaktirastu tathā''vayōḥ॥  
mā sma putrāḥ praṇaśyantu mā dhanaṁ mā kulakramaḥ।  
agnayō mā praṇaśyantu gr̥habhaṅgastu mā''vayōḥ॥ ityētē mantrāḥ।  
ēvaṁ prasādya pūjāṁ ca kr̥tvā lakṣmyāstathā harēḥ।  
candrāyārghyastathā dēyō dadhyakṣataphalādibhiḥ।  
arghyamantraḥ---  
gaganāṅgaṇasandīpa kṣīrābdhimathanōdbhava।  
bhābhāsitadigābhōga ramānuja namō'stu tē॥ iti।  
naktaṁ praṇamyāyatanē hariṁ bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ।  
brāhmaṇāya dvitīyē'hni śayyā dēyāśca dakṣiṇāḥ॥  
yāni tatra mahābāhō kālē santi phalāni ca।  
madhurāṇi na tīvrāṇi na cāpi kaṭukāni ca॥  
dātavyāni nr̥paśrēṣṭha svaśaktyā śayanē'nagha।  
madhurāṇi ca datvā tu manōvallabhatāṁ vrajēt।  
tasmātkaṭukatīvrāṇi strīliṅgāni ca varjayēt॥  
kharjūramātuliṅgāni sthitēna śirasā saha।  
(sthitēna śirasā dr̥ḍhanārīkēlaphalēnētyarthaḥ।)  
ētānyēva tu viprasya gāṅgēya sahitāni ca॥  
dvitīyē'hni pradēyāni bhaktyā śaktyā ca bhārata।  
vāsōdānaṁ tathā dhānyaṁ phaladānasamanvitam॥  
ēvaṁ karōti yaḥ samyaṅnarō māsacatuṣṭayam।  
saptajanmatrayaṁ vīra gr̥habhaṅgō na jāyatē॥ iti।  
pādmē---  
gītavāditranirghōṣaṁ dēvadēvasya kārayēt।  
ghaṇṭā vādyamaśaktasya sarvavādyamayī yataḥ॥  
ēvaṁ sampūjya gōvindamaśnīyāttailavarjitam।  
naktamakṣāralavaṇaṁ yāvanmāsacatuṣṭayam॥  
tataḥ prabhātē sañjātē lakṣmīpatisamanvitām।  
dīpānnabhōjanairyuktāṁ śayyāṁ dadyādvicakṣaṇaḥ॥  
pādukōpānahacchatracāmarāsanasaṁyutām।  
abhīṣṭōpaskarairyuktāṁ śuklapuṣpāmbarairvr̥tām॥  
sōpadhānakaviśrāmāṁ phalairnānāvidhairyutām।  
tathā''bharaṇadhānyaiśca yathāśakti-samanvitām॥  
avyaṅgā gauśca viprāya vaiṣṇavāya kuṭumbinē।  
dātavyā vēdaviduṣē na bakavratinē kvacit॥  
tatrōpavēśya dampatyamalaṅkr̥tya vidhānataḥ।  
patnyāstu bhōjanaṁ dadyādbhakṣyabhōjyasamanvitam॥  
brāhmaṇasyāpi sauvarṇīmupaskarasamanvitām।  
pratimāṁ dēvadēvasya sōdakumbhāṁ nivēdayēt॥  
ēvaṁ yastu pumānkuryādaśūnyaśayanaṁ harēḥ।  
na tasya vittavirahaḥ kadācidapi jāyatē।  
nārī vā vidhavā rājanyāvaccandrārkatārakam। iti।  
mātsyē---  
na virūpaṁ na śōkārtaṁ dampatyaṁ jāyatē kvacit।  
na putrapaśuratnāni kṣayaṁ yānti dvijōttama॥  
saptakalpasahasrāṇi saptakalpaśatāni ca।  
kurvannaśūnyaśayanaṁ sūryalōkē mahīyatē॥ iti।  
asmin candrōdayē pūjāvidhānāccandrōdayavyāpinyēva tithi grāhyā। dinadvayē'pi tatsattvāsattvayōḥ paraiva।  
caturṣvasitapakṣēṣu māsēṣu śrāvaṇādiṣu।  
aśūnyākhyaṁ vrataṁ kuryājjayayā tu phalādhikam। iti vacanāt।

8f721c4eb2.b: Observed on Śukla-Pañcamī tithi of Caitraḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
8f721c4eb2.s:
śuklāyāmatha pañcamyāṁ caitrē māsi śubhānanā।  
śrīrviṣṇulōkānmānuṣyaṁ samprāptā kēśavājñayā॥  
tasmāt tāṁ pūjayēt tatra yastaṁ lakṣmīrna muñcati।  
ēṣā śrīpañcamī kāryā viṣṇulōkagatipradā॥
